exposure: Type of abdominal scars (transverse cesarean sectioning, midline scars, laparoscopic scars, appendectomy scars, abdominal total hysterectomy scars, umbilicus scar)
outcome: Scar-related perfusion complications in DIEP flaps
Conversion rate from DIEP to ms-TRAM flap
Need for venous superdrainage with SIEV
Acute donor site complications (poor wound healing)
cohort: The study included 273 breasts from 267 patients who underwent DIEP flap breast reconstruction between October 2008 and April 2022.
finding: Pre-existing abdominal scars, including cesarean section scars, do not compromise DIEP flap transfer nor increase the incidence of late fat necrosis, although transverse scars were associated with significantly less SIEV availability.
